Consult Summary:
- Patient Ayrton Warren (DOB 16 May 1982) assessed remotely for an acute left-sided headache that began this morning; differential includes tension-type headache vs migraine; conservative analgesia, workplace/time-off and lifestyle measures recommended with follow-up in one week.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Acute onset severe left-sided headache that woke the patient from sleep today at approximately 05:30.
  - Headache persists at time of consult.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Woke early this morning with pain (~05:30). Normally rises at ~07:00.
  - Has a prior history of headaches that were less severe and typically localized to the front of the head rather than one-sided.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Slight worsening on initially lying down (takes time to get comfortable); overall feels better when lying down.
  - Paracetamol taken this morning with little or no benefit (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Associated symptoms:
  - Mild photophobia: bright lights make eyes sore but tolerable.
  - Brief dizziness on first getting up this morning that has since resolved.
  - No nausea reported.
  - No neck stiffness, no fever.
- Relevant psychosocial contributors:
  - Significant work-related stress for about 2 months with many late nights; patient reports anxiety related to workload.
- Systems review / pertinent negatives (as reported):
  - No fever, no persistent nausea, no neck stiffness.
  - No suicidal ideation (explicitly denied).
  - No known prior diagnosis of hypertension; patient reports never having had BP checked.

Past Medical History:
- Anxiety — duration ~2 years; patient reports being on sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- No other medical conditions reported.
- No history of diagnosed migraines in the family (patient reports none).
- Family history: mother has history of anxiety; no other physical illnesses reported in family.

Medications:
- Sertraline — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Paracetamol — taken this morning (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Ibuprofen — recommended by clinician (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies reported.

Social History:
- Living situation: lives with partner.
- Tobacco: non-smoker.
- Alcohol/substance use: not discussed/not documented.
- Pets: has a cat.
- Exercise: typically runs approximately three times per week.
- Diet: describes diet as "OK," not unhealthy.
- Work: currently under increased stress and late nights for approximately two months.

Family History:
- Mother: history of anxiety.
- No family history of migraines or other physical illnesses reported.

Physical Examination:
- No physical examination documented (remote consultation; no vitals provided).

Investigations:
- No investigations, imaging, or blood tests performed or reported during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute left-sided headache — differential includes tension-type headache (favored by stress and anxiety history) and migraine (supported by unilateral pain and photophobia).
  - Plan:
    - Start ibuprofen (medication recommended; dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Patient may continue paracetamol if desired (already taken and reported as not very effective).
    - Advise minimum 7–8 hours sleep nightly.
    - Advise fluid intake 1.5–2.0 liters daily (excluding coffee/tea).
    - Recommend considering short period off work (suggestion: one week self-certification) to reduce stress.
    - Provide link to local counselling service for self-referral; counselling recommended.
    - Provide link/summary in notes about headache danger signs and when to re-present.
    - Follow-up arranged in one week with clinician or another GP; earlier contact if symptoms worsen or new concerning features develop.
    - If no improvement on this plan, consider blood tests or further investigations (to be arranged at follow-up if indicated).
- Issue 2: Anxiety (chronic, on sertraline).
  - Plan:
    - Continue current management (no medication change documented).
    - Recommend counselling/self-referral (link to be provided).
    - Suicide/self-harm screening: patient denies current thoughts of self-harm.
    - Monitor mental health at follow-up or sooner if concerns arise.
- Issue 3: None additional specifically diagnosed in this consult.
  - Plan:
    - Safety net: recontact earlier for worsening symptoms; clinician to leave danger-signs information in notes.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature) not recorded.
  - Neurological/physical examination not performed or documented.
  - Exact medication doses, routes, and frequencies for sertraline, paracetamol, and recommended ibuprofen not documented.
  - No documentation of alcohol use quantity or other substance use.
  - No objective tests (e.g., blood tests, imaging) performed.
  - No explicit documentation of occupational details beyond "stress/workload" (e.g., job type).
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Patient name confusion: patient initially said "Atan" then supplied full name "Ayrton Warren"; clinician also used "Anthony" once — conflict noted regarding name used.
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Overall clear and intelligible; minimal background noise. Occasional brief pauses and filler words present but did not obscure clinical content.
